title: Franz Liszt's birth chart
metaDescription: Franz Liszt's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 28.1° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mars holds a sextile to Uranus at 0.6° — close enough to weld drive to disruption. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 28.1° into Libra — the third decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 11.6° Libra, Venus holds 0.8° Scorpio, Mars holds 17.3° Capricorn — in the old shorthand, thought that travels by comparison; attraction that works by atmosphere; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars and Uranus hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.6° wide. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Mars sextile Pluto at 0.9°, and Uranus trine Pluto at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. The Sun in Libra at 28.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Scorpio at 0.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Capricorn at 17.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Cancer at 6.3° is in exaltation. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 water, 2 air, 2 fire, 1 earth by element and 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed by mode. Water weights a chart toward the felt and the remembered — information that arrives as atmosphere before it arrives as words. Pluto was retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.2° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
